PMEX manages all of it, with E/M coding reviewed against the clinical documentation before every claim leaves the department.

ED E/M Level Coding

Levels 99281–99285 coded from clinical documentation per 2021 MDM complexity.

Critical Care Billing

99291 + 99292 coded from documented critical care time in the chart.

Observation Status Coding

Correct Type of Bill and observation CPT codes applied per patient status.

Procedure Coding

Laceration repair, cardioversion, intubation coded alongside E/M with modifier -25.

Critical Care Add-Ons

Sound Familiar?

Common Emergency Medicine Billing Problems, and How PMEX Fixes Them

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

ED level 4 documented but billed as level 3, MDM complexity not fully captured.

PMEX codes every ED E/M from 2021 MDM criteria, problems, data reviewed, and risk, not from a default template.

Critical care time documented as "1 hour", 99292 add-on unit never billed.

PMEX aggregates all critical care documentation entries and bills 99292 when total time exceeds 74 minutes.

Observation vs. inpatient status miscoded, wrong Type of Bill on the facility claim.

PMEX coordinates observation and inpatient status coding with the facility team before submission.

Procedure codes not submitted on same-day ED visits, bundled into E/M incorrectly.

PMEX identifies every same-day procedure and submits it alongside the E/M with modifier -25.

Trauma activation fee not billed, facility charges not coordinated with physician billing.

PMEX coordinates trauma activation billing with the facility team to ensure both claims are consistent.

Moderate sedation not separately billed on procedural ED visits.

PMEX bills moderate sedation (99152-99153) separately on every qualifying procedural visit.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Emergency Medicine Billing, and How PMEX Fixes Them

ED practices lose 15–25% of revenue to E/M under-coding, critical care documentation gaps, and procedure bundling errors.

PATTERN 01

ED Level Under-Coded, Level 3 Billed When Level 4 or 5 Supported

Patient: chest pain, EKG, troponin, imaging. MDM supports 99285 (level 5, $240). Billed as 99284 ($185). $55 per visit. In a 200-visit/day department with 30% under-coding: $3,300 daily in systematic revenue loss.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX codes every ED E/M against 2021 AMA MDM criteria, number of problems, data reviewed, and risk. Level selected from documentation, not from a default template.

PATTERN 02

Critical Care Time Not Aggregated, 99292 Add-On Missed

Physician documents critical care at 8:00 AM (30 min) and 11:00 AM (35 min), total 65 minutes. 99291 billed. 99292 not billed, billing team does not aggregate across entries. $120 per critical care case missed.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX aggregates critical care time across all documentation entries for the same patient on the same calendar day, billing 99292 when total time exceeds 74 minutes.

PATTERN 03

Laceration Repair Not Billed, Bundled into E/M

Laceration repair (12001, $180) performed in ED alongside E/M. Only E/M submitted. Modifier -25 not applied. Repair code never submitted. In a department with 15 daily lacerations: $2,700 daily in unbilled procedure revenue.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX identifies every procedure from clinical documentation and submits the procedure code alongside the E/M with modifier -25, confirmed that documentation supports a separately identifiable E/M service.

Questions

Emergency Medicine Billing Questions Answered

Using the 2021 AMA Medical Decision-Making framework: number and complexity of problems, amount and complexity of data reviewed, and risk of complications. We code from MDM documentation, not the old history/exam element method.

Per CMS, critical care time is cumulative for the calendar day. All separately documented critical care episodes are aggregated. We add all documented time and bill 99291 for the first 30–74 minutes and 99292 for each additional 30 minutes.

We manage the professional fee billing and can coordinate with the facility billing team to ensure observation status, inpatient status, and procedure codes are consistent across both claims.

Yes, ventilator management (94002-94003), CPR (92950), and other separately billable critical care services are billed alongside the critical care E/M with correct bundling rules.

Per the 2023 CMS final rule, we apply split/shared billing rules based on who performs the substantive portion of the visit, documented in the chart.

Claims submitted within 24–48 hours of encounter documentation being finalized. Same-day submission is standard for high-volume ED groups.
